subject: Conditional commit schedule, MAP milestones and SLA offsets
messages:
From: Alex T. <alex.t@edgescale.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@edgescale.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation next steps + MAP / SLA ask

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency numbers on the 8k model. Before we move into a formal pilot, procurement and our CTO want a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a clear statement of how SLA/latency SLOs will be tied to commercial concessions (discounts / credits).

High level asks from our side:
- A two-week pilot with performance goals and telemetry access.
- A ramp-to-commit schedule (we expect to move to a reserved commit if pilot meets targets).
- Clarity on pricing tiers and how discounts scale with commit size and timelines.
- Explicit SLA targets for production and a credit schedule if SLOs are missed.

Can you share a MAP template and a proposal that ties discounts/credits to milestone completion? If possible, include typical latency SLOs you’d guarantee for committed customers (p95/p99 numbers and whether they vary by model variant).

I’ve looped in procurement for timing. Looking to close a paper trail by early November if the pilot goes well.

—Alex
Alex T. | Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeScale
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex T. <alex.t@edgescale.com>
Cc: procurement@edgescale.com, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation next steps + MAP / SLA ask

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a draft MAP and an SLA redline to start (EdgeScale_MAP_v2.pdf; SLA_draft_redline.docx).

Summary of what we’re proposing (short):
1) Pilot (2 weeks) — evaluation criteria: throughput at target QPS, p95 latency <= 250ms for the standard generation path, and pass of basic quality checks supplied by EdgeScale. We’ll provide telemetry export (pilot-telemetry-10-22.csv) and a dedicated Slack channel for realtime triage. Pilot discount: 15% off hosted rates for pilot usage.

2) Ramp & commit — MAP milestone schedule:
   - Week 0–2: Pilot
   - Week 3–6: Expanded pilot + load test (10–30% production traffic)
   - By Week 8: Finalize commit decision and contract signature
If EdgeScale signs a 12-month reserved commit within 30 days of pilot completion, we propose a tiered discount: 10% @ baseline commit, +5% for each 2x increase in committed QPS (capped at 30%).

3) SLA / latency SLOs and concessions:
   - Base production SLO (for committed customers on the baseline model variant): p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 600ms (measured at the tenant edge for gen-8k workload).
   - If EdgeScale accepts our recommended caching & batching profile and commits to a 4-week ramp to target QPS, we will tighten the committed p95 to 160ms.
   - If we miss the agreed p95/p99 for two consecutive weeks, Redwood will provide service credits: 5% monthly credit for p95 misses, 10% for p99 misses, escalated review and remediation plan.
   - For any SLA miss where Redwood is unable to meet remediation, we will provide an additional one-time onboarding credit equal to 1 month of average usage (as a commercial concession).

4) Trade-offs: Lower latency SLOs require reserved capacity, a pinned model variant, and acceptance of our recommended tokenization/caching approach. If EdgeScale wants loose commit terms, latency guarantees will be relaxed and the discount profile adjusts accordingly.

Next steps: please review attachments and let me know which commit tier you expect to target (baseline / 2x / 4x). If you want the p95 tightened to ~120–140ms we can explore a Dedicated capacity proposal (separate pricing).

I’ll loop in Marcus (CS lead) to coordinate the MAP checklist and Priyom (SE) for telemetry specifics.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alex T. <alex.t@edgescale.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@edgescale.com, Jill Moreno <jill.m@edgescale.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation next steps + MAP / SLA ask

On Wed, Oct 21, 2026 at 10:04 AM lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Summary of what we’re proposing (short):

Thanks Lauren — that is very helpful. A few clarifications/asks from EdgeScale:
- Would you consider tightening the p95 in the standard (hosted) offer to 150ms rather than 160ms if we agree to a 9‑month commit (instead of 12)? That helps our execs for the Q4 launch.
- Can the credit schedule be structured so procurement can claw back up to 20% in credits for repeated SLA misses (we can accept a cap).
- We’d like telemetry access to include sampled traces (not just aggregates) for the pilot; is that possible?

We’ll aim for the pilot starting next Tuesday. Procurement will take a look at the MAP PDF and SLA redline and get back with standard redlines.

—Alex
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Alex T. <alex.t@edgescale.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation next steps + MAP / SLA ask

Alex — quick technical note on meeting tighter p95 targets.
- Surface-level: hitting 150ms p95 on hosted shared pools is feasible with the baseline gen-8k variant if the request distribution follows the pilot profile and you accept the caching profile we suggested (5–10s prefix cache, token-level KV).
- If your live traffic has a higher tail (many long contexts, streaming enabled), the safe path is Dedicated capacity (isolated GPUs) or a pinned quantized variant.
- We can give sampled traces for the pilot via a temporary telemetry export (PSV) — will attach a small sample after first day of pilot.

Attaching a short technical checklist in the MAP doc for engineering: model variant, max seq len, expected token distribution, warmup rules, and fallback variant.

—Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Alex T. <alex.t@edgescale.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation next steps + MAP / SLA ask

Alex / Lauren — security quick-check:
- EdgeScale asked about telemetry and traces. We can provide sampled traces but we need a signed data-processing addendum (DPA) that limits retention and access scope.
- SOC 2 evidence: we’ll share our latest report under NDA — please tell me who on your team should receive it.
- MAP note: ensure the MAP does not request any model internals or weights — telemetry is fine but not model artifacts.

If you want the p95 tightened under hosted, we’ll also include a clause requiring pinned versions and an agreed cache warmup plan — otherwise we can’t guarantee the tighter SLO.

—Neha
Head of Security | Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex T. <alex.t@edgescale.com>
Cc: procurement@edgescale.com, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation next steps + MAP / SLA ask

Alex / team — summary + ask to lock timelines.

1) What we can sign today (conditional):
   - MAP v2 with pilot starting 2026-11-09 (2 weeks). EdgeScale will provide test corpus and target QPS.
   - Pilot telemetry + sampled traces (temporary export) after NDA / DPA is in place.

2) Commercial conditionality (if pilot passes):
   - If EdgeScale signs a 9-month commit within 30 days of pilot completion at the 2x commit tier, Redwood will:
       • tighten p95 production SLO to 150ms (hosted, baseline model variant)
       • increase committed discount by 5 percentage points (i.e., baseline discount + an extra 5%)
   - If EdgeScale opts for 12-month commit and Dedicated capacity, we’ll offer p95 120–140ms and an additional 10% discount on reserved rates.

3) SLA credit schedule (final draft will be in the contract):
   - Single-week p95 miss: 5% monthly credit.
   - Two consecutive weeks p95 miss: 10% monthly credit + account review.
   - Repeated breaches (3+) over quarter: escalation to exec sponsor + negotiated remediation credits (up to 20% cap).

4) Next actions for EdgeScale:
   - Procurement: review SLA_draft_redline.docx and send redlines to legal@edgescale.com by Nov 10.
   - Sign DPA (we’ll send standard form) to enable sampled traces.
   - Confirm target commit tier (baseline / 2x / 4x) by Nov 12 so we can prepare dedicated capacity if needed.

I’ll prepare a one-page mutual action checklist and a DocuSign envelope for the MAP + DPA if you confirm the timeline. If you want the tighter 150ms commitment on hosted for 9 months, confirm the 9-month length in reply and procurement signoff timeline mentioned above.

Thanks — looking forward to getting pilot scheduled.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: EdgeScale_MAP_v2.pdf; SLA_draft_redline.docx; pilot-telemetry-10-22.csv
